description.summary: tell shell components when a workspace switch is animating

protocol.description:
A workspace switch is animated by the compositor: the windows of the old workspace give way to the new ones over a configurable transition. Shell components are not part of that animation — a panel, dock or launcher is a layer surface that stays where it is — so their contents change the instant they learn the workspace changed, which reads as a snap in the middle of an otherwise smooth switch.
This protocol tells them when the switch is animating and how long it lasts, so they can fade their own contents across it instead. The compositor is the only party that knows: it owns the animation, its curve and its duration, and the duration is configuration a client cannot see.
The transition is reported as a start and an end rather than as a series of phases. A client that wants to swap its contents at the least visible moment computes that moment from the start event's duration against its own clock, which needs no further round trips and stays smooth if an event is late. The end event exists so a client can settle exactly rather than guessing, and a client that misses it is only left finishing its own animation on its own schedule.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the testing phase. Backward compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward incompatible changes can only be done by creating a new major version of the extension.

interface.name: workspace_transition_manager_v1
interface.description:
Binding this global is the whole opt-in: the compositor sends transition events to every bound client. There is no per-surface object because a workspace switch is a property of the session rather than of any one surface — every shell component animating it is animating the same event.
Events are not sent for a switch that does not animate (the compositor transitioning instantly, or a switch to the workspace already active). A client therefore cannot rely on a start event for every workspace change, and should continue to treat its own source of the active workspace as the truth about which one that is.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Informs the server that the client will no longer use this global. No further events are sent after this request.

event.name: started
event.description:
Sent when the compositor begins animating a switch away from one workspace and towards another.
`duration_ms` is how long the compositor's own animation will take. A client fading its contents should treat it as the window it has, rather than choosing a duration of its own: the two are meant to look like one movement, and the compositor's is configurable.
`from` and `to` are workspace identifiers in the same namespace the client already uses to name workspaces. `from` may be empty when the compositor was not showing a workspace before this one.

event.name: finished
event.description:
Sent when the animation started by the matching started event has completed. A client that is mid-fade can settle on its final state.
A switch interrupted by another switch produces a finished event for the first before the started event for the second, so start and finish always pair up.
